findings.claim: The hostile-reader route table lists theorem rows with public status no-send, `Claim-ledger blockers` = `0`, Lean certificates, Lean refs, finite positives, and negative controls.
findings.failure_mode: The compact table still enables theorem theater: `0` blockers plus Lean certificates can be cited as theorem readiness even though the current claim ledger keeps the rows release_promotion_allowed=false and scientific_promotion_allowed=false. A hostile reader can reduce this to formal-methods/GSN assurance packaging rather than a promoted OC theorem surface.
findings.required_repair: Rename `Claim-ledger blockers` to `adversarial_review_blocker_total`, add explicit `release_promotion_allowed=false`, `scientific_promotion_allowed=false`, and `fresh_cerberus_required=true` columns, and label Lean evidence as `consistency-check evidence only` in the compact table.

findings.claim: T133-CYCLE: `Promoted eligible-live status requires an explicit cycle mode or non-vacuous maintenance predicate.`
findings.failure_mode: The row is marked no-send with scientific_promotion_allowed=false, but the claim text itself uses promotion wording. The current lint rule only constrains `promotion_condition`, so a no-send wording violation remains in the public claim field and can be read as autopoiesis/dynamical-systems liveness promotion rather than a formal release-consistency check.
findings.required_repair: Rewrite the claim as `Within the no-send formal release-consistency check, eligible-live classification requires an explicit cycle mode or non-vacuous maintenance predicate`, and extend the promotion-wording lint to `claim`, `scope_limit`, and hostile-reader guide text.

findings.claim: T133-MIN: `Within the declared v12 release tuple semantics, each promoted tuple component has a one-field semantic keep/drop witness that changes the release verdict.`
findings.failure_mode: No theorem row is release-promoted or scientifically promoted, so `promoted tuple component` conflicts with the ledger posture and inflates a classifier-internal keep/drop regression into a minimality claim. This is reducible to requirements traceability/V&V coverage unless promotion language is removed.
findings.required_repair: Replace `promoted tuple component` with `declared no-send tuple component`, state that the keep/drop witness is only a classifier regression test, and block display of T133-MIN as minimality evidence until a release-promoted tuple exists.

findings.claim: Comparator `bounded_positioning_note` fields identify residual OC differentiators such as release-governed control plane, typed identity blocker, K-level demotion, and provenance-style gate stack.
findings.failure_mode: The register correctly does not promote uniqueness, priority, or absence, but it still itemizes residual differentiators after illustrative single-source checks. Against systems engineering, assurance cases, GSN, provenance systems, and formal methods, these residuals are plausibly known traceability/governance patterns with OC labels.
findings.required_repair: Downgrade all residual-delta wording to `candidate local integration description, not searched for novelty`, and add explicit reduction-to-prior-art tests for assurance case, GSN, V&V, provenance, and formal-methods comparators before retaining any differentiator language.
